HTML, SVG, XML and JavaScript are refused with 415 (`file type not allowed`) on every upload path (POST /api/_upload, POST /api/_files and a multipart POST /api/<table>, which then creates no row): by content for HTML and XML, and by extension for .html, .htm, .xhtml, .svg, .svgz, .xml, .js, .mjs. The hosted platform's media storage also refuses .shtml and a file with no extension (size_limits). Executables and scripts (.exe, .sh, binaries) are NOT refused: like every type outside images, audio/video, pdf, txt, csv and json they are served as a download (Content-Disposition: attachment) with nosniff; on the CDN backend a script-killing CSP is layered on too.

The served content type comes from the stored file's extension, not from the Content-Type the client sent, and nothing checks that the bytes match the name: PDF bytes uploaded as `scan.png` are served as image/png. Every upload is served with `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, so a browser does not guess another type. Check the type in your own code where it matters.
PRIVATE files are never directly fetchable: use `bm.signedUrl(ref, { record })` or a flow ending in `run: serve_file` (api({at:'flows'})). Don't hand the raw URL to the browser.
Don't assume the returned reference is `/uploads/...` - under the platform CDN backend it's a full https://<cdn>/... URL. Store + render whatever the upload returns.

Each file is capped at 50 MB and a multipart body at 51 MB unless MAX_UPLOAD_BODY_BYTES raises it (see size_limits); over either answers 413. On the hosted platform the total is capped too, by the owner account's media storage allowance (see storage_allowance: 507 `storage cap reached` with code `media_storage_limit`); a self-hosted app has no total quota.
delete_upload is intentionally unavailable over HTTP/SDK; invoke it only inside a server flow after an authorization-scoped lookup.
